biography: Nicolò Piancastelli, born under the Tuscan sun in 1990, wasn't bred for the racetrack. His family owned a vineyard, expecting him to inherit the family business. But the roar of engines always called to him louder than the rustle of grapevines. His passion ignited during a local hill climb where he saw an aging Lancia Stratos conquer the asphalt. He begged his father for a kart, finally receiving one for his 14th birthday. Nicolò quickly outgrew local karting, showing a remarkable aptitude for car control and race craft. He transitioned to single-seaters but lacked the funding to climb the traditional ladder. Instead, he found his niche in GT racing, impressing Lamborghini scouts with consistent pace and tactical brilliance in a regional endurance series. Now in his early thirties, Piancastelli pilots a Lamborghini Huracan GT3, a respected, if not yet legendary, competitor in the GT world. He's known for his methodical approach and unflappable demeanor, a stark contrast to the fiery Italian stereotype. While a world championship eludes him, Nicolò continues to be a consistent points scorer, a testament to his skill and perseverance.
drivingStyle: Piancastelli is a study in precision and calculated aggression. He doesn't typically overdrive the car, preferring to extract maximum performance through meticulous corner entry and exit. His tire management is exceptional, often running longer stints than his competitors. He excels under pressure, rarely making mistakes when the stakes are high. He is known for his defensive driving, making it extremely difficult for opponents to overtake him, even if they have a pace advantage. His style is often described as 'clinical' and 'efficient,' a far cry from the flamboyant flair often associated with Italian drivers.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, gifted to him by his grandmother before his first professional race.
Listens to classical music (specifically Vivaldi) in the paddock to calm his nerves before each session.
Meticulously cleans his steering wheel with a microfiber cloth before every race, a ritual he says helps him 'connect' with the car.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about who's fastest for a lap; it's about who's smartest for a race."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Daytona in the GTD class in 2020. It was a hard-fought victory, with Piancastelli executing a flawless final stint, holding off a charging rival to secure the win for his team.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2021 with only two hours remaining. A mechanical failure sent him into the barrier, ending his team's hopes for victory and leaving him visibly shaken.
